purpose: Locate the confidence collapse of checkpoint local_atomic_seed17 by replaying the engineering survey and the frozen in-domain maze cohorts through the same local service, and separating in-domain from out-of-domain confidence behaviour.

verdict.label: uncertain only out-of-domain (engineering-judgement survey); the model does emit well-separated, positively-calibrated confidence inside its own maze domain
verdict.statement: The collapse is not global. Inside the trained maze task family the checkpoint produces a distinct high-confidence mode: 90/240 (37.5%) of test+ood questions carry confidence >= 0.9 and those are 97.8% correct, confidence is positively associated with correctness (point-biserial r = +0.397), and ECE is 0.085 (test) / 0.073 (ood). On the 13 natural-language engineering questions the whole distribution is compressed into [0.255, 0.736] with median 0.505 - entirely below the in-domain median 0.779 and below every in-domain high-confidence question - so 13/13 fall under the 0.9 gate and the gate's abstention there is a domain-transfer failure, not a global absence of confidence. Alternative (a) is rejected (confidence is not low everywhere). Alternative (c) is rejected in-domain (confidence is positively and monotonically related to correctness there, accuracy 97.8% at >=0.9 vs 65.3% below 0.9); (c) has only weak, n=6 support inside the survey itself and that support does not reproduce the prior doc's rank claim. The honest residual: separation is incomplete - 100/240 (41.7%) in-domain questions sit at or below the survey's maximum confidence, and in-domain abstention at 0.9 is still 62.5%, so the 0.9 gate abstains on most in-domain questions too; it is the *confidence mode* that is missing out-of-domain, not the abstention.

what_is_not_established: n=6 fixed-answer survey questions cannot support a calibrated anti-correlation claim; the 'confidence vs correctness' statement for the survey is a direction on a 3/3 split.

The engineering survey contains no in-domain analog for its question *format* (natural-language criteria over 3-4 named options) - so this measurement cannot say whether the collapse is caused by the language distribution, the choice/score question types, the option wording, or the state length. Only that it is out-of-family.

No per-question confidence from a context-filter / retention decision was measured here; the maze boolean questions are a different question type from the gate's removal decisions, so the 62.5% in-domain abstention at 0.9 is not a direct prediction of the gate's removal rate.
No checkpoint other than local_atomic_seed17 was measured, and nothing was trained or tuned - the diagnosis is about this checkpoint's confidence geometry only.

The 0.5-0.6 and 0.8-0.9 in-domain accuracy buckets are small (51 and 20 questions pooled) and the 0.8-0.9 bucket is locally non-monotone (65.0% accuracy); the monotone story is carried by the >=0.9 bucket.
